data.narrative:
Tempo is a Series A-stage climate and energy technology company founded by Nima Rahmatian, Kelvin Randhir, Joerg Petrasch, and Alessandro Bo. The valuation analysis draws on a broader climate and energy sector universe of nine comparable companies—one public (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix—though the scarcity of direct same-stage comparables limits peer-median approaches.

Given insufficient narrow-peer density (fewer than three same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation characteristics), the stage-progression method provides the primary analytical anchor. Using total capital raised of $50M as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, this method implies a valuation of $100M. This multiplier reflects typical investor dilution and value accretion between Series A and subsequent funding rounds within early-stage climate tech.

The triangulated range derived from available quantitative methods supports a valuation band of $85M to $115M, with a median of $100M. The analysis reflects material uncertainty: the single-method foundation means the range rests primarily on stage-based progression rather than cross-validated peer comparison. Investors should weight confidence accordingly and monitor emergence of additional comparable transactions within the climate tech sector to refine future estimates.
